The primitives form a coherent system for evaluating predictive accuracy through hit rate estimation, calibration error tracking, and sample size validation. Hit rate estimator computes empirical success rate as H = k/N, enabling probabilistic inference under binomial assumptions. Calibration error tracker evaluates consistency between predictions and observations via E_cal = E[|p_pred - p_obs|], capturing miscalibration. Sample size validator enforces statistical validity by flagging segments with insufficient data. These operators interlock in a dual structure: GSI leverages them for Bayesian updating and conformal inference, while GSE uses them for dynamic belief revision and state transition logic. Failure modes include low N leading to unstable estimates, high E_cal indicating systemic bias, and misalignment between prediction and observation. The system supports retroactive correction through confidence intervals and adaptive thresholds.
